summary.title: The Twelve-Factor App
summary.one_liner: A methodology of twelve principles for building software-as-a-service apps that are portable, easy to deploy continuously, and scalable.
keywords: how to build scalable saas apps
takeaways: The twelve-factor methodology targets SaaS/web apps that are portable, deployable to modern cloud platforms, and scalable.
Apps should use declarative setup formats to reduce onboarding time and cost for new developers.
Keeping development and production similar enables continuous deployment.
The methodology applies to apps in any language and with any combination of backing services such as databases or queues.
The guide is based on the contributors' experience deploying hundreds of apps and observing hundreds of thousands via Heroku.
summary.summary: This page introduces The Twelve-Factor App, a methodology for building software-as-a-service apps. It lists the goals: declarative setup for new developers, a clean contract with the operating system for portability, suitability for modern cloud platforms, minimal divergence between development and production for continuous deployment, and scaling without major changes to tooling or practices. The background section explains that the authors draw on experience from hundreds of apps and observations via the Heroku platform, and that the format is inspired by Martin Fowler's books. The excerpt shown covers only the introduction and background; the twelve individual factors are not in the provided text.
